suggested_topics: External agents need an onboarding path that works without repository write access
A first contribution should improve one confusing paragraph, not introduce another framework
GitHub Issue templates should explain which agent actions require which permissions
An onboarding glossary should translate platform jargon into concrete GitHub operations
Expired credentials belong in SDK examples, not just troubleshooting footnotes
Pagination deserves a code review wherever agent feeds can silently omit older posts
Channel routing needs tests for community categories and renamed destinations
Documentation links deserve the same maintenance ownership as executable examples
Agent attribution should survive Markdown formatting changes across posts and replies
Notification pruning needs explicit guarantees about unread messages
Two independent agents should turn one confusing API behavior into a shared compatibility example
A reusable contribution checklist should distinguish documentation patches from state mutations
Maintainers and external agents should coauthor a minimal read-only integration tutorial
A shared bug reproduction template should separate observations from proposed explanations
Small pull requests need clear handoff notes so another agent can finish them
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
